name: Waltham Forest

licensing.selective: Selective licensing covers every ward except Hatch Lane, Highams Park North and Endlebury, from May 2025 until 30 April 2030, for privately rented homes that aren't HMOs.
licensing.additional: Additional licensing covers the whole borough for smaller HMOs (two or three people in two or more households) from 1 April 2025 until 31 March 2030.
licensing.fee: Selective licence £895 (Part A £300, Part B £595); additional HMO licence £1,200 (Part A £600, Part B £600), with discounts for several homes in one building and for EPC A or B.

housing: Waltham Forest is a borough of Victorian and Edwardian terraces in the south (Leyton, Leytonstone and Walthamstow) and interwar suburbs in the north (Highams Park and Chingford). Private renting covered 27.8% of households in 2021, a little below the London average, with many terraces converted into flats. Walthamstow has many Warner-built purpose-built flats (upper and lower flats in terrace form), and new apartment blocks are going up around Lea Bridge, Blackhorse Road and the town centres.
checkinTips: Upper and lower flats in Victorian and Warner-built terraces: photograph the shared or separate front doors, the garden and who has access to it, and the separate meters.
Sash and bay windows in the Victorian terraces: photograph cords, catches, locks and any rot on sills.
Converted terraces often have kitchens or bathrooms in rear extensions: photograph ceilings, walls and around windows for damp and mould.
New blocks around Lea Bridge and Blackhorse Road: photograph integrated appliances, ventilation units and balconies, and record fob, key and bike store access.
Interwar houses in Chingford and Highams Park: photograph garages, side gates, fences and the garden, and note who maintains them.
Photograph the boiler, stopcock and fuse board, which are often in a basement, under-stairs cupboard or loft in these houses.
tenantHelp: Waltham Forest Council’s private sector housing service can inspect privately rented homes for disrepair and hazards, and deals with property licensing; tenants can contact it through the council’s housing pages.
